title: Maximum Non Negative Product in a Matrix
summary: Given a m x n matrix grid, starting from the top-left corner (0, 0), find a path to the bottom-right corner (m - 1, n - 1) such that the product of the integers along the path is maximized and non-negative.
statement: Given a m x n matrix grid, starting from the top-left corner (0, 0), find a path to the bottom-right corner (m - 1, n - 1) such that the product of the integers along the path is maximized and non-negative. You can only move right or down in the matrix. The product of the path should be calculated, and if it is non-negative, return the product modulo 10^9 + 7. If the product is negative, return -1.
constraints: 1–15 rows and columns; each value is from -4 through 4.
Move only right or down. Return -1 when every path product is negative; otherwise return the maximum modulo 1,000,000,007.
hints: A negative cell swaps the roles of best and worst prefix products.
Store both the maximum and minimum product reaching every cell.
Combine both extrema from the upper and left cells, multiply by the current value, and retain the new extrema.
Every path enters from above or left; two extrema suffice because multiplication is monotone or reverses order based on sign.
editorial: Every path enters from above or left; two extrema suffice because multiplication is monotone or reverses order based on sign.

tests.explanation: Every top-left to bottom-right product is negative, so return -1.
The best nonnegative path has product eight.
